newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO will have no second-class members - Solana.
newsitem.headline: NATO will have no second-class members - Solana.

text.p: NATO Secretary General Javier Solana stressed on Monday that no second class members of the military alliance would be created as it expands to former foes from behind the old Iron Curtain.
"I want this to be very clear. There won't be any second class members," he told reporters after meeting Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski.
Poland has been anxious that NATO should not agree on a watered-down NATO membership for new entrants to meet Russian objections that the pact's enlargement threatens its security.

He said last Friday's Helsinki summit between U.S. leader Bill Clinton and Russia's Boris Yeltsin had boosted optimism over the relationship between NATO and Russia and the possibilities of striking an accord between the two before a July NATO summit launches its expansion project.
Moscow has deep reservations about NATO's plans to expand eastwards to its former allies and to appease it the alliance is seeking to offer it a charter to cement a new partnership.
"I think that we are capable of having a joint text before the summit," Solana said.
Kwasniewski, whose country sees full, rapid NATO entry as a top policy goal, said the Helsinki meeting had brought NATO expansion closer.
"After Helsinki we are nearer to the enlargement than before," he said.
Poland expects to be among the first countries, with Hungary and the Czech Republic, to be asked at the Madrid summit to start NATO entry talks and to join in 1999.
